maria-cs: FYI customer acct_0A12 reporting dashboard vs invoice mismatch for Feb 28 reconciliation. Dashboard export shows ~147k tokens, invoice line shows ~192k. Can someone triage?
kevin-billing: got invoice id?
maria-cs: invoice_2026_02_28_489 — customer attached screenshot of dashboard vs PDF. says spike around 23:58 UTC.
billing-bot: Invoice generation finished: invoice_2026_02_28_489 — line_items: tokens=192345, plan=pro-250k, total=$1234.50
ashley-fin: can you drop the dashboard CSV export link?
maria-cs: https://s3.redwood/prod/exports/acct_0A12/feb28_dashboard.csv :eyes:
dan-eng: quick note — we shipped a streaming count change in commit abc123 on Mar 1 that de-dupes some streaming flushes. Feb 28 was before that. possible double-count from reconnects.
kevin-billing: running quick reconciliation query now.
kevin-billing: ```sql
SELECT sum(tokens) as tokens, status
FROM billing.events
WHERE account_id='acct_0A12' AND date_trunc('day', ts) = '2026-02-28'
GROUP BY status;
```
kevin-billing: results: 192320 total tokens, statuses: 200=158k, 499=28k, 503=6k
maria-cs: 499 = client aborted? customer reported reconnects during a long stream.
dan-eng: yes 499 = client_aborted. We started including aborted-request tokens in raw invoice counting for reliability, but dashboard aggregation historically excluded them. That explains gap.
ashley-fin: so invoice is "raw events" and dashboard is "filtered/aggregated". Need to decide policy: credit or keep invoice as-is.
maria-cs: customer asks for full credit on the 28th window — they think duplicates inflated billed tokens.
kevin-billing: quick calc: if we subtract aborted tokens (28k) at our token rate $0.00065/token -> ~$18.20, hmm math off vs invoice delta. But there are also partial tokens from truncated requests and system tokens.
dan-eng: also saw ~320 requests that retried, producing multiple event records per user action. sample log snippet:
```
2026-02-28T23:57:59Z request_id=rx9 status=499 tokens=1280 path=/v1/generate
2026-02-28T23:58:00Z request_id=rx9 status=200 tokens=1150 path=/v1/generate
```
dan-eng: that pair is a duplicate for same request_id after reconnect; both were counted in raw invoice. dashboard dedupe dropped the 499 line.
ashley-fin: policy historically: invoice = raw usage, dashboard = best-effort UX view. For credits we look for system bugs or miscounts due to server-side duplication. This looks like a server-side dup introduced before the de-dupe fix. So eligible.
kevin-billing: I'll draft a credit memo: propose credit $420 to cover the duplicate window and fees. Opening ticket and flagging ops for fix confirmation.
dan-eng: I will backport the de-dupe logic to the billing pipeline for historical filtering and add a metric to detect >=1% 499 token ratio per-day. Will also post a short incident note.
maria-cs: customer wants ETA for credit and confirmation that future bills won't repeat. can we give short timeline?
ashley-fin: I'll approve credit if ops confirms duplicate-count root cause. Target: credit issued within 3 business days.
kevin-billing: created ticket TICKET-4021 and assigned: ops -> @dan-eng, finance -> @ashley-fin, cs -> @maria-cs.
billing-bot: Support ticket created: TICKET-4021 (acct_0A12) — priority: P2
maria-cs: sending customer provisional update now: "we identified duplicated aborted requests that were included in invoices for Feb 28; we're issuing a credit and rolling preventive fix." :thumbsup:
kevin-billing: after fix, we should surface a new dashboard line for "raw vs deduped token counts" so customers see both.
dan-eng: agreed. I'll add the metric and a backfill job to compute deduped totals for the last 90 days.
maria-cs: thanks team. I'll close the thread with the customer once credit posts.
